sb_prompt: WHAT HOBBIES DO YOU HAVE IN YOUR SPARE TIME?  DO THEY INCLUDE ANY HANDICRAFTSWOODWORKING?
turns: So, I'm a librarian actually, and I've always loved books, though I kind of realized that years ago I wasn't sure exactly why I picked it as my career. Do you have any hobbies? Do you do any woodworking?

Oh wow, that's deep, I actually do have some hobbies but I'm mostly just bad at them honestly, and no, I don't do woodworking at all, though my cousin does that stuff and it... yeah, it's actually pretty scary watching him work with wood.
Yeah, that's actually kind of intense, but I get why it's so satisfying to see it come together, I just can't build stuff myself. Do you knit or sew anything, or is it mostly just reading?
Oh mostly just reading, honestly I can't be bothered with needles, but honestly I do love organizing stuff at work... wait, that might be boring?
Oh no, don't worry, organizing is actually my favorite thing to do, it's so calming to just sort everything out!

Oh really? That actually sounds super therapeutic, I was worried you'd think work stuff was just mundane, and honestly, organizing my little section at the pharmacy does feel like solving a puzzle sometimes, even if the stuff itself is kinda yucky.
Yeah, it totally makes sense, I love that you see it like a puzzle, but sometimes I feel like I just get too caught up in the dust bunnies hiding under the shelves to actually finish organizing!

Haha, totally get that, it's like fighting a losing battle against the dust sometimes! I mostly just try to group things by color or expiry date to make it look neat, but yeah, sometimes I feel like the boxes just slide back into chaos before I can even finish the labels.
Yeah, that color sorting is actually genius, I swear I've been hunting for books by genre for years and they just keep migrating back to random spots!
Haha, totally! But honestly, I think the books are just more excited to be out there than I am to put them back.

Haha, that's a fun way to put it! I feel like my fiction section is definitely having a midlife crisis every morning. Do you ever get any weird customers at the pharmacy, like people who just stare at the flu shots for twenty minutes?
Yeah, that happens all the time, like last week a lady was just staring at the shingles vaccine and wouldn't stop asking if it was a scam until I actually showed her the pamphlet!
Haha, that's terrifying! I actually had a guy last week who asked if the Dewey Decimal System was a code for alien messages.
Haha, I can totally relate, I had a guy ask if the flu shot was going to turn him into a zombie yesterday!
Haha, don't worry, you're the first person to ask me that, I thought I was the only one! So what about you, do you ever have customers who ask if the medicine will turn them into a zombie too?
Haha, okay, I promise no zombies, just a lady who wanted me to prescribe her antibiotics for a cold, which I literally just said "no" to!
Haha, that is the most logical thing I have ever heard! You're absolutely right, you can't just hand out antibiotics for a cold, that's how superbugs are made! Did she argue about it at all?
Yeah she kinda argued about it for a bit but I stuck to my guns and just sent her home with some OTC stuff instead.
Haha, glad she listened, but did she actually leave or just argue while you called the doctor?
She didn't really argue, she just looked kind of defeated and left, though she did ask if I had any throat lozenges on the way out.

That's actually a relief, throat lozenges are way safer than fighting a losing battle, though I do have to be careful with the tea recommendations too since some people think chamomile cures everything!
Haha, I feel like I need a badge for that, "I Know What I'm Talking About," because half the time I'm just guessing on the side effects myself!
Haha, trust me, half the time I'm just guessing about the tea too! But at least if I mess up, I don't have to worry about legal trouble, right?

Haha, fair point, I guess my license is my only safety net! But honestly, sometimes I still feel like I'm walking on thin ice with the staff here, especially when I need to tell people "no" without being mean... it's weird balancing all these conflicting feelings.
Yeah, I get that, it's so hard to tell people no without feeling like you're kicking them when they're down, but sometimes you just have to trust your gut and hope they listen.
Yeah, it really is, sometimes I feel like I'm walking on eggshells when I have to say no to someone who's just really desperate for relief.

Yeah, that eggshell thing is exactly what I feel sometimes, like if I tell a patron they can't check out a banned book, I'm basically going to get fired or something, so I end up just sighing and hoping they understand.
Yeah, I mean, it's just exhausting sometimes, like everyone thinks you're some kind of villain if you say no, but I honestly just need to protect myself too.
Yeah, I guess it's just about knowing when to draw the line so you don't end up looking like the bad guy.
Yeah, I guess that's the only way to keep it all together without burning out.
Yeah, it's definitely that balance thing, you just have to find your own line before you burn out.
Yeah, I guess once I just start saying no to stuff that feels wrong, things get a little easier, even if the guilt stays for a bit.
Yeah, I think finding that line makes all the difference, even if that little bit of guilt never really goes away.
Yeah, honestly, the guilt usually fades after a while, or at least I try to convince myself it does, even if it lingers for a few days.
Yeah, I guess for me it's mostly just about hoping people understand that saying "no" is actually a way to keep things safe for everyone, even if it feels heavy right now.
Yeah, I guess once the dust settles, the weight feels a little lighter, even if you know it might come back tomorrow.
Yeah, that makes sense, I guess once the dust settles the weight feels a little lighter too.
Yeah, exactly, maybe I'll just go grab a coffee and pretend I'm not thinking about any of it right now.
Maybe I should stop being such a drama queen and just go get that coffee before I actually do burn out.
Haha, fair enough, I guess I'll head out too before I actually lose my mind.
